Load/save dispatcher.
Purpose: select the save path when A=$53 and the load path otherwise, then perform the KERNAL file operation and restore game state.
Inputs: A is the command character; filename and state buffers are already prepared.
Outputs: saved or loaded state; runtime vectors and display state restored.
Assumptions: KERNAL ROM and I/O can be banked in.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, KERNAL workspace.
Hardware changes: switches $01 banking and calls KERNAL PLOT, SETLFS, SETNAM, LOAD/SAVE.

Save serializer: copies 106 bytes $2406-$246F, then visits all 34 database entries and appends byte zero (flags/type) from each of 546 object records. Record length at +8 advances the source; directory traversal uses $05D8/$05EC. Native execution stopped before $04F6 produces exactly 652 bytes at the work-buffer root $10A0/$10A1, compared byte-for-byte with an independent database walk. A separate native disk-device-8 SAVE/LOAD round trip on a private copy of the contributor image writes EST  .CM and reads all 652 payload bytes back exactly.

Load deserializer after KERNAL success and $EA signature check: copies 106 bytes into $2406-$246F, then restores byte zero of each of 546 database objects in directory order. Native execution stopped at $05A8 restores all 652 independently generated test bytes exactly; record sizes remain unchanged because only flags/type byte zero is replaced. $05A8 then adjusts sprite-enable bits using $2467. The disk-device-8 SAVE/LOAD round trip reproduces the payload exactly; with IRQs masked for the final comparison, all 106 state and 546 object flags are restored. Tape transfer is untested.

Initializes area offset pointer from $109E/$109F and area count from database byte $9D00. Falls through $05EC with Y=$FF to select the first directory word. Shared by save and restore; both controlled native traversals visit 34 areas and 546 records.

Increments directory-byte index, reads one little-endian base-relative area offset via ($7A), adds database base $109C/$109D, stores object count from header +1 at $0411, and advances object pointer $7E/$7F by eight. Saves directory position at $0413. Native serializer/deserializer both reproduce the independent directory order.

Advances object pointer $7E/$7F by total record length read at +8, restores directory index Y from $0413 and decrements remaining object count $0411. Native save and restore tests traverse all 546 exact object boundaries without changing their length bytes.

KERNAL-vector restoration bridge.
Purpose: copy the 32-byte canonical vector table from KERNAL ROM $FD30-$FD4F to RAM $0314-$0333, then install CHROUT=$86CF and NMI=$7579.
Inputs: standard C64 KERNAL ROM.
Outputs: restored RAM vectors, custom output/NMI hooks, sprites disabled.
Assumptions: $01=$37 selects KERNAL ROM and I/O.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags.
Hardware changes: masks IRQs during the copy, writes $01, $0314-$0333, and VIC sprite-enable $D015.

Retained 53-byte startup routine, not sprite artwork. SEI, port $38, X=0; reads each of four physical RAM pages $D800-$DBFF, temporarily decrements port to $37 to write the corresponding colour hardware address, then increments it back. Iterates all 256 X values, leaves port $38 and jumps to $473B initialization. A controlled native run with hardware colours initially zero reaches $473B and reproduces every one of the 1024 shadow low nibbles; physical shadow stays unchanged. Presence is unchanged across entry/menu/play snapshots; this call test establishes its operation, not a fresh loader invocation trace.

459 consecutive zero bytes $C235-$C3FF following the retained palette-copy routine ending with JMP $473B at $C232. Identical at cold hand-over, menu and gameplay. The initial sprite pointer table selects offsets $000-$1C0 in bank $C000, so this tail is outside its eight selected slots. Described as captured zero padding; no blanket claim about all possible future readers/writers is made.

SID_UPDATE_ONE_VOICE ($CA11-$CF1A; command continuations $CF79-$CFBD)
Purpose: interpret one voice's order/pattern commands, select instrument/frequency, advance note/gate/duration and modulation state, and prepare the seven SID-register shadow bytes used by the outer tick.
Inputs: current voice $C809=0-2, SID register offset $C808=0/7/14, stream positions/pointers $C80A+ and $F7-$FC, and initialized player tables/state $C806-$C884.
Outputs: advances one voice's shadow bytes, counters, and pointers. Normal paths return through $CAE4/$CC7F/$CC9E/$CF1A. A global end marker clears $C806 and all three voice controls, deliberately discards its direct caller's return address, and exits the enclosing tick.
Assumptions: stream/table pointers and command encoding are valid; $CF1B-$CF78 is the separate SID initializer, while $CF79-$CFBD are noncontiguous command-tail continuations. Musical names for individual proprietary commands are not claimed without score tracing.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, extensive $C806-$C884 state, self-modified operands $CA55/$CF7C/$CF8B/$CFA6, dispatch bytes, and stack on global-end escape.
Hardware changes: command $A0 can clear selected voice control $D404 plus offset 0/7/14; global end clears $D404/$D40B/$D412. The outer tick $C885-$CA10 performs the normal $D400-$D418 flush.

Four-byte-spaced order command branch slot, JMP $CFB4 at $CA9D. Preceding NOP padding $CA9C and mutable branch operand $CA98 form the dispatch layout. Order command dispatch JMP $CF79 at $CAA1, selected by rewritten relative branch $CA97/$CA98. Handler reads next order byte into per-voice frequency offset $C83F and increments order index. Adjacent four-byte slots dispatch transpose, wait and instrument remapping.

Final branch of the self-modified order-command dispatch beginning $CA86: JMP $CF97 remaps one of eight instrument slots. $CAA8 then handles ordinary order entries as phrase indices through split directory $0D07/$0D3C. Phrase decoder $CAC1 handles wait $A0, filter voice mask $A1/$A2, pitch slide commands $C0-$FE, vibrato $90-$BF, instrument $80-$8F and note bytes below $80. Notes include following duration byte; $FF ends a phrase, returning to the order list. This is a continuation inside the player, not a separate initialization routine.

Instrument command low nibble plus voice base (0,8,16) indexes remap table $1017. Remapped byte selects a ten-byte record based at $0F15: pulse high/waveform/ADSR and effect parameters are loaded into channel state. Resets pulse, waveform and modulation counters and advances phrase position by one before parsing the next command.

Immediate operand of ADC at $CB5B, rewritten to 0,8,16 by the three-voice tick dispatcher. Added directly to instrument command low nibble, it selects the corresponding remapping slot at $1017; the static captured value sixteen is the third voice base, not an additional constant. Continuation reads ten bytes of instrument state from $0F15 plus remapped offset. Default offsets increase by nine, so these access windows overlap by one byte. This is a mutable operand, not a separate routine.

Adds transpose $C80D+voice and twenty to the note byte, indexes split frequency tables $065A/$06BA, adds fine offset $C83F, and sets gate bit. Reads duration from the following phrase byte and advances position by two. Initializes configured waveform, pulse, vibrato and slide counters; note duration is installed at $C830+voice.

Per-tick continuation for an active note. Clears gate at release point, honors voice suppression delay, decrements duration, applies configured pitch slide unless the global synchronization flag is set, and updates pulse modulation from $0FDA. This continuation keeps state in per-voice triplets and cached seven-register groups. Native SID output and song completion remain separate tests.

SID_PLAYER_INITIALIZE ($CF1B-$CF78)
Purpose: reset the three-voice player and install the requested selector offset for subsequent SID ticks.
Inputs: A is the selector value; zero is valid for initialization/reset; resident SID tables and the $102F-$1046 seed state are installed.
Outputs: stores six times the selector in $C813; gate-pulses then clears all three voice-control registers; clears player state $C806-$C884 as encoded, restores seed bytes into $1017-$102E, initializes self-modified player pointers $F7-$FC, and leaves player state/volume byte $C806 and $C82C at $0F.
Assumptions: selector multiplication addresses the verified per-selector player layout; writable self-modifying and state storage is available.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $F7-$FC, $1017-$102E, and $C806-$C884; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: writes $01 then $00 to SID voice-control registers $D404, $D40B, and $D412; it does not change SID master volume $D418.

SID_READ_CURRENT_VOICE_STREAM_BYTE ($CFC0-$CFD3)
Purpose: read the byte at the current per-voice pattern position.
Inputs: X voice index 0-2; current offset $C810, X; stream pointers ($F7/$F8), ($F9/$FA), and ($FB/$FC).
Outputs: A is the selected stream byte, Y is the current stream offset, and X is preserved.
Assumptions: the voice index and all stream pointers are valid.
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags only.
Hardware changes: none.

Four-byte constants 01,02,04, FF at $CFD4-$CFD7 after phrase-read helper and before sound-request entry $CFD8. Dispatcher uses the first three as per-voice selections; final $FF is a separate sentinel. Exact consumer/index domain remains open; do not assign this occupant as executable instructions.

SID_INITIALIZE_IF_ENABLED ($CFD8-$CFE3)
Purpose: request a one-shot sound only when the game's sound/music gate permits it.
Inputs: requested zero-based sound index in A; gate byte $123A.
Outputs: when $123A is zero, increments A to the player's one-based index and tail-calls SID initializer $CF1B; otherwise returns without changing the player.
Assumptions: callers use Castle's internal sound indexes.
Clobbers: X and, on the enabled path, registers/state clobbered by $CF1B.
Hardware changes: enabled path initializes SID player state; later ticks write $D400-$D418.
Evidence: branch, increment and tail transfer observed; caller sound identities independently verified.

SID register clear.
Purpose: silence/reset the first 20 SID registers.
Inputs: none.
Outputs: $D400-$D413 cleared to zero.
Assumptions: Caller-established runtime state described in Inputs is valid.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags.
Hardware changes: writes SID voice/filter registers $D400-$D413; master volume $D418 is not part of this loop.

Physical RAM image of the 1000 initial bitmap third colours at $D800-$DBE7, followed by 24 zero padding bytes. At cold hand-over, all 1000 bytes exactly match the low nibbles of hardware colour RAM read with I/O visible. The RAM shadow is unchanged in menu/play while the game writes colour hardware separately. This is initial authored palette data retained under I/O; a CPU STA $D800 with port $35 addresses the colour chip, not this RAM allocation. The VIC consumes hardware colour RAM rather than reading this shadow as sprite/bitmap pixels.

Second 256-byte page of physical RAM colour shadow, colour cells 256-511 (40-column cell index). Startup $C200 reads this page with port $38 and writes all low nibbles to hardware colour RAM with port $37. Controlled native copy from initially zero hardware matches all 1024 entries and leaves the shadow unchanged. These RAM bytes are authored initial colours, distinct from I/O at the same CPU addresses.

Third 256-byte page of physical RAM colour shadow, cells 512-767. $C21B reads RAM while port=$38; $C220 writes hardware colour RAM while port=$37. The controlled loader test matches every entry. Cell 765 has its own $DAFD HUD annotation; physical RAM and I/O occupy different banks despite matching numeric addresses.

Initial third-colour RAM shadow cell at character column 5, row 19, corresponding to matrix $C6FD and physical x40-47, y 152-159. The shadow continues through $DBE7 with padding afterward. At cold hand-over its low nibble matches hardware colour RAM. A CPU store at $DAFD with I/O visible writes the colour chip; $61A8 can leave its patched operand equal to this address after completing the fifteenth viewport row.

Fourth 256-byte shadow page. First 232 bytes supply cells 768-999 of the initial 40x25 third-colour plane; last 24 at $DBE8-$DBFF are zero padding. Native startup-copy test covers the whole page and confirms hardware low-nibble output and unchanged physical RAM. $C225 reads this page with RAM visible, $C22A writes it with I/O visible.
Twenty-four zero bytes $DBE8-$DBFF after the 1000 initial third-colour shadow bytes beginning $D800. They are outside the 40x25 colour plane, and remain zero across cold entry, menu and settled play.

KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF43 ($FF43-$FF47) - inactive copied-KERNAL bytes, not executed by this occupant.
Classified data, not code. These five bytes are a verbatim copy of the KERNAL's pre-dispatch
sequence (PHP / PLA / AND #$EF / PHA) left in RAM by an earlier phase. In the captured menu
occupant nothing reaches them: they carry zero incoming references, and the only live entry into
the copied dispatcher is the hardware IRQ/BRK vector at $FFFE/$FFFF, which points directly at
$FF48. Modelling them as executable would assert a control-flow path the capture does not contain.
Banking: at the capture $01=$35, so $E000-$FFFF is RAM with KERNAL ROM banked out; these bytes are
physical RAM, and the same RAM is the VIC bank 3 multicolor bitmap ($E000-$FF3F) plus its tail.
See KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF5B for the rest of the residue and IRQ_DISPATCH for the live dispatcher.

IRQ_DISPATCH ($FF48-$FF5A)
Purpose: implement the copied KERNAL common IRQ/BRK dispatcher by saving A/X/Y, testing the stacked Break flag, and transferring through the appropriate RAM vector.
Inputs: a hardware IRQ/BRK frame or compatible synthetic frame on the stack; RAM vectors $0314/$0315 and $0316/$0317 are installed.
Outputs: jumps indirectly through $0316 for Break set or $0314 for Break clear after pushing A, X, and Y.
Assumptions: the selected handler follows the copied KERNAL convention and restores the three saved registers before RTI; physical RAM at $FF48 is the active occupant when KERNAL ROM is hidden.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and stack until the selected handler restores them.
Hardware changes: none directly; the all-RAM IRQ/BRK vector $FFFE/$FFFF points here.

KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF5B ($FF5B-$FF7F) - inactive copied-KERNAL bytes, not executed by this occupant.
Classified data, not code. Decoded as instructions these bytes read as the KERNAL's post-dispatch
tail (JSR $E518, raster wait on $D012, $D019 acknowledge, CIA 1 $DC0D/$DC0E setup, JMP $EE8E), but
every one of those targets lies inside $E000-$FF3F, which at this capture is the VIC bank 3
multicolor bitmap - image data, not routines. Disassembling them therefore manufactures call and
jump edges into pixels. Nothing in the captured occupant references this range.
Banking: $01=$35 banks RAM under BASIC and KERNAL while leaving I/O visible, so the CPU sees these
RAM bytes rather than KERNAL ROM. The program reaches genuine KERNAL routines only by first
setting $01=$37, after which the ROM's own jump table executes and these RAM bytes are irrelevant.

Retained physical RAM bytes $FF5E-$FF80 exactly match the corresponding 35 bytes in the emulator KERNAL ROM. They continue the IRQ service/wait code after dispatch $FF48. Live ROM/RAM comparison confirms byte identity; it does not establish which loader copied them or that every entry is called. Keep RAM/ROM bank meanings distinct; ROM itself is not shipped.

Copied KERNAL jump table ($FF81-$FFF5) - inactive RAM residue, classified data.
These bytes duplicate the KERNAL's documented entry table (CINT, IOINIT, SETMSG $FF90,
SETLFS $FFBA, SETNAM $FFBD, LOAD $FFD5, SAVE $FFD8, PLOT $FFF0, ...). They are NOT what executes
when the program calls those addresses. At this capture $01=$35, so $E000-$FFFF is RAM; a call to
$FFD5 in that state would run these RAM bytes, whose JMP operands point into $E000-$FF3F - the VIC
bank 3 multicolor bitmap. The program instead sets $01=$37 before any KERNAL call, banking ROM in
so the ROM's own table runs; these RAM copies are then invisible.
They are therefore kept as data with their public entry labels and per-entry contracts retained as
bank-qualified logical API annotations: the labels document where the program calls, and the
incoming references from the program are real, but no outgoing flow is asserted from these bytes.
The three-byte $6C xx 03 entries ($FFC0 OPEN, $FFC3 CLOSE, $FFCF CHRIN, $FFD2 CHROUT, ...) are
indirect through the $0300-$0332 RAM vector page and are likewise inert here.
